{{Quote|Black Leader, there's a brand new hole in that oscillator. Looks like our friends got in.|Yolo Ziff, to Poe Dameron|<ref name="Episode VII" />}}
'''Yolo Ziff''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[artist]] who flew for the [[Resistance]] during its [[Cold War|conflict]] against the [[First Order]]. In [[34 ABY]], Ziff created [[propaganda]] for the Resistance, and he participated in the [[Battle of Starkiller Base]], flying under the command of [[Black Leader]] [[Poe Dameron]]. During the battle, the [[Resistance pilot]]s targeted [[Starkiller Base]]'s [[thermal oscillator]], a weak point in the [[superweapon]]. Although their weapons were not strong enough to cause any damage to the structure, Ziff spotted a hole in the oscillator, which had been created by Resistance members [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]], who were on the [[planet]]'s surface. With the new opening, Ziff and the other [[pilot]]s renewed their attack on the oscillator, and Dameron destroyed the target, crippling the weapon.

==Biography==
===Propaganda artist===
A [[human]] [[Gender|male]], Yolo Ziff was a talented [[holographer]], digital editor, [[Artist|illustrator]], and [[starfighter]] [[pilot]].<ref name="Propaganda">''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]''</ref> By [[34 ABY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> Ziff joined the [[Resistance Starfighter Corps|Starfighter Corps]] of the [[Resistance]], a military group formed by [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] to protect the [[New Republic]] from the [[First Order]]. During Ziff's service, [[Resistance pilot]]s joked that if [[Black Leader]] [[Poe Dameron]] were to pose for a poster, recruitment numbers would increase. Drawing inspiration from the quip, Ziff created a faux [[propaganda]] poster titled [[Resistance (poster)|''Resistance'']], which pictured a gallant image of Dameron standing in a "clear [[Atmosphere|sky]] full of promises," joined by the [[X-wing starfighter|X-wing fighters]] under his command. Although the poster was intended as a prank, it ended up on the [[HoloNet]], resulting in multiple new recruits.<ref name="Propaganda" />

Following his unintentional success, Ziff was commissioned by Organa to create a piece to help the New Republic understand the true intentions of the First Order. The subject of the poster was to be the [[attack on Tuanul]], a village slaughter witnessed by Dameron. Ziff hastily illustrated ''[[The Massacre at Tuanul]]'', depicting [[First Order flametrooper|flametroopers]] in [[Tuanul]], setting [[fire]] to the settlements of peaceful religious pilgrims. Ironically, by the [[time]] Ziff finished the piece, the First Order, using a secret [[superweapon]] called [[Starkiller Base]], destroyed the New Republic [[capital]] of [[Hosnian Prime]].<ref name="Propaganda" />

===Assault on the Starkiller===
{{Quote|Dropping out of lightspeed.|Yolo Ziff, prior to the assault on Starkiller Base|<ref name="Episode VII" />}}
Immediately after the [[Hosnian Cataclysm]], the First Order targeted [[D'Qar]], the [[planet]] of the [[Resistance base]]. When the Resistance learned of the First Order's imminent attack, they formed a plan to disable Starkiller Base's [[thermal oscillator]]—a critical weak point—hoping to destroy the weapon. However, the planet was [[Deflector shield|shielded]], so [[Finn]], a former [[First Order stormtrooper|First Order strormtrooper]], volunteered to escort [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]] inside the base, where they could disable the shield.<ref name="Episode VII" /> In preparation for the [[Battle of Starkiller Base|assault]], Ziff and the other [[Resistance pilot]]s were told to expect at least 80 percent casualties.<ref name="CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref>

[[File:X-Wings_Starkiller_Divebomb.png|thumb|left|250px|Yolo Ziff participated in the Resistance's assault on Starkiller Base.]]
Ziff, flying with [[Red Squadron (Resistance)|Red Squadron]] and [[Blue Squadron (Resistance)|Blue Squadron]], entered [[hyperspace]] under the leadership of Dameron. Once the ground team disabled the shield, Dameron was given authorization to begin the assault, and he relayed the command. Ziff acknowledged Dameron's signal, and the [[squadron]]s dropped out of [[lightspeed]], following Dameron into the planet's atmosphere and switching the [[S-foils]] of their [[T-70 X-wing starfighter]]s into attack position. Once the squadrons reached the oscillator, Dameron gave the order to fire, so Ziff and the other pilots launched [[proton torpedo]]es at the structure. Despite hitting their target, no damage was done, and squadrons of [[TIE/fo space superiority fighter]]s engaged them. The dogfight pushed the battle into the planet's [[orbit]], and the First Order starfighters overwhelmed the Resistance pilots.<ref name="Episode VII" />

On the surface of the planet, Solo and Chewbacca had seen an opportunity to assist the pilots, so they set explosives inside the structure of the oscillator. When the charges were detonated, a opening was created, which Ziff soon noticed. He informed Dameron of the change, and the [[commander]] gave an order to resume their attack on their target. As the pilots flew toward the oscillator, Dameron told the remaining pilots to cover him as he entered the structure via the opening created by Solo and Chewbacca. From inside, Dameron destroyed the building, and the Resistance pilots followed him away from the planet as the damage caused it to implode.<ref name="Episode VII" />

==Personality and traits==
[[File:Yolo_Ziff_Resistance_poster.jpg|thumb|right|150px|As a prank, Ziff created a propaganda poster featuring Poe Dameron.]]
A human male, Ziff had [[Color|blue]] [[eye]]s and light-colored skin.<ref name="Episode VII" /> Ziff was a gifted holographer, digital editor, and illustrator, so when he heard a joke about Dameron posing for a poster, Ziff pulled a prank on the commander by actualizing the piece.<ref name="Propaganda" />

==Equipment==
As a pilot in the Resistance, Ziff flew a T-70 X-wing starfighter,<ref name="Episode VII" /> a starfighter model manufactured by the [[Incom-FreiTek Corporation]].<ref name="ICS">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> During the assault on Starkiller Base, Ziff wore a [[flight suit]] and a [[flight helmet]] with red and gray markings.<ref name="Episode VII" /> His [[astromech droid]] was [[M9-G8]].<ref name="Flight Log" />

==Behind the scenes==
Yolo Ziff was created for [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']], the seventh installment of the episodic ''[[Star Wars]]'' saga,<ref name="Episode VII" /> which was released on [[December 18]], [[2015]].<ref name="Release Date">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-episode-vii-to-open-december-18-2015|text=Star Wars: Episode VII to Open December 18, 2015}}</ref> His helmet was designed by [[J.J. Abrams]]' son [[Henry Abrams|Henry]].<ref name="Commentary">Director [[J.J. Abrams]] [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']] commentary</ref> The film was written by [[Lawrence Kasdan]], J.J. Abrams, and [[Michael Arndt]], and Ziff was portrayed by actor [[Stefan Grube]],<ref name="Episode VII" /> who also served as the editor for the film's first two trailers.<ref name="Grube">{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/star-wars-the-force-awakens-easter-eggs|text=The Ultimate Guide To Star Wars: The Force Awakens Easter Eggs|author=Peter Sciretta|date=2016-12-22|archivedate=20200109163153}}</ref> Following the film's release, Ziff appeared in ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'', a [[LEGO]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] adaptation of the film.<ref name="LEGO">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]''</ref> However, Ziff is absent from the film's [[Star Wars: The Force Awakens (novelization)|adult]] and [[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: A Junior Novel|junior novelizations]], in which his role is filled by Poe Dameron.<ref name="Novel">[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Awakens'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="Junior">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: A Junior Novel]]''</ref> Additionally, Ziff's role is taken by [[Temmin Wexley]] in [[The Force Awakens Adaptation 6|''The Force Awakens Adaptation'' 6]], a [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] adaptation of the film's final scenes.<ref name="Comic">[[The Force Awakens Adaptation 6|''The Force Awakens Adaptation'' 6]]</ref>
